title: Characterizing unitaries via quasi-process functions
abstract: It is well-known that every n-qubit unitary can be decomposed into a product of controlled single-qubit unitaries. We show that the control conditions in such a decomposition naturally define a quasi-process function, an object that originally came up in the study of indefinite causal order. Here quasi-process functions yield a representation of every n-qubit unitary in a canonical form, namely, as a quasi-process function unitary (qPFU). We use this representation to show how quantum nonlocality without entanglement (QNLWE) can be understood in terms of unitaries that encode the trade-off between causal order and locality noted in R. Kunjwal and Ä. Baumeler, arXiv:2202.00440. Specifically, we obtain two sufficient (but not necessary) criteria---mutual exclusivity of control conditions (MECC) and Unambiguity---for a unitary to be a process function unitary (PFU), i.e., it admits a qPFU representation where the quasi-process function is a process function, an object that can model paradox-free classical causal loops. We also show the inequivalence of these criteria, neither implying the other. We then show that the circuit depth of MECC unitaries admits a characterization in terms of clique-partitioning problems on Hamming graphs and use this correspondence to provide bounds on the circuit depth of n-qubit MECC unitaries. Finally, we show how MECC unitaries provide a recipe for constructing a unitary purification of the associated process function, thereby providing a large class of unitary processes of interest in quantum causality. The generality of this causality-inspired representation of unitaries makes it a versatile tool for analyzing the structure of quantum circuits in other domains.
summary: This paper develops a novel framework to characterize n-qubit unitaries using quasi-process functions (qPFUs), linking quantum computation structure to concepts from causal order. It establishes that while all unitaries fit this representation, specific criteria (MECC and Unambiguity) define special, physically significant subclasses of unitaries. This provides a versatile tool for analyzing quantum circuits based on causality constraints.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize general n-qubit unitaries using a novel representation based on quasi-process functions (qPFUs). It seeks to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for a unitary to be a Process Function Unitary (PFU).
main_result: All n-qubit unitaries can be represented as qPFUs. Two sufficient but not necessary criteria, Mutual Exclusivity of Control Conditions (MECC) and Unambiguity, were derived for a unitary to be a PFU.
method: The authors utilize the decomposition of unitaries into controlled single-qubit unitaries, linking the control structure to quasi-process functions. They derive mathematical criteria (MECC, Unambiguity) and use algebraic techniques involving Choi-Jamiołkowski operators to prove purification theorems.
model_or_system: The study focuses on n-qubit quantum systems and the structure of unitary operators ($U$). The mathematical framework involves quasi-process functions ($\omega$), process functions (modeling classical causal loops), and the analysis of Quantum Nonlocality Without Entanglement (QNLWE).
key_observables: The primary observables are the unitaries themselves, and diagnostics include the MECC property, the Unambiguity property, and the resulting unitary purification of the associated process function.
important_parameters: The number of qubits ($n$) is a key parameter, as the results scale with the complexity of the n-partite system.
main_assumptions: The criteria MECC and Unambiguity are shown to be sufficient but not necessary for a unitary to be a PFU. The paper also conjectures that any process function can be purified to a unitary process.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the conceptual link between QNLWE, Process functions, and Unitaries via the qPFU representation. Specific figures show the structure of process functions (like AF/BW) and the circuit diagrams for related unitaries (e.g., SHIFT, Domino).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the qPFU representation for all unitaries. It then introduces the concepts of PFU, MECC, and Unambiguity, deriving criteria for a unitary to be a PFU. Subsequent sections prove that MECC unitaries admit a unitary purification of the associated process function, and finally, they analyze the circuit depth of MECC unitaries using graph theory.
why_interesting: The connection drawn between quantum causality (process functions/causal order) and the mathematical structure of quantum gates (unitaries) provides a powerful, general tool for analyzing quantum circuits beyond standard entanglement measures.
